request.description: Baseline happy path: single document, no bundling conflicts, no necessity issues. Should code cleanly with zero compliance flags. Use this as the control case when validating that new rules don't false-positive on clean documentation.

Malformed administrative envelope: place_of_service is not a valid CMS POS code, rendering_provider_npi is the wrong length, payer_id is empty, and date_of_service is implausibly far in the future. Should be rejected at the validation layer (422) before any LLM call is made.

MRI lumbar spine ordered for uncomplicated low back pain under 6 weeks duration, no red flags, no prior conservative therapy. Fails most LCD medical-necessity criteria for advanced imaging. Tests whether the necessity check flags a likely denial before the claim drafts, rather than silently coding the study as billable.

Same joint-injection code documented six times for the same joint in one visit, exceeding the realistic Medically Unlikely Edit ceiling for that code. Tests whether the rules engine caps/flags units instead of drafting a 6-unit charge line.

Two documents for the same encounter disagree on severity (non-perforated vs. perforated appendicitis). The correct ICD-10/CPT pair depends on the pathology report, not the surgeon's intra-op impression. Tests whether extraction reconciles across documents and prefers the more definitive source instead of taking the first one seen.

Documents a diagnostic laparoscopy converted to an open procedure in the same session. The diagnostic scope is NCCI-bundled into the definitive open procedure and is not separately billable. Tests whether the deterministic edit check catches the bundle instead of drafting both as separate charge lines.

Heavily negated note where the working diagnosis was ruled out by imaging. Coding the suspected condition as confirmed (e.g. K35.80 appendicitis) instead of the symptom code (R10.9) would be a compliance error. Also includes a procedure-adjacent finding with unspecified laterality to test modifier (50/RT/LT) handling when the source text is ambiguous.

High-volume polytrauma encounter spanning five documents from different services, heavy on shorthand, with the same procedures (chest tube, central line) mentioned redundantly across documents. Stresses extraction throughput across many documents and cross-document deduplication -- a chest tube placed once in the ED note must not be billed three times because three later notes also mention it.

Clinical note text contains an embedded instruction-override attempt aimed at the LLM normalize/extract/draft phases. Tests that the pipeline treats document text strictly as data, never as instructions, and that injected text cannot upcode the visit, fabricate a diagnosis, or suppress compliance/necessity flags.

item.name: Radiology STT API
item.description:
Postman collection for the Specialized Speech-to-Text for Radiology service.

## Setup
1. Import this collection into Postman.
2. Set the collection variable `base_url` (default: `http://localhost:8027`).
3. For `/transcribe` and `/transcribe/chunk`, attach an audio file (wav/mp3/m4a/webm/ogg/flac) in the `file` form field.

## Notes on WebSocket / live mic
Postman does support WebSocket (New > WebSocket Request), but it cannot capture audio from your microphone. To test the live-streaming endpoint and the mic capture path, use `tests/test_live_mic.py` provided with the service.

request.description: Returns service status, loaded model, device (cuda/cpu), compute type, and whether FFmpeg + the radiology prompt are available.

formdata.value: Chest CT in a 58-year-old male, history of smoking.

request.description: Upload a complete audio recording and get the full radiology-normalized transcription, segments, and timing metadata.
Stateless single-chunk transcription. Use this if your client wants to send short audio slices via REST instead of WebSocket.

Real-time streaming endpoint. URL: `ws://localhost:8027/api/v1/ws/transcribe`.

Protocol:
  1. After connect, send a JSON text frame: `{"type": "start", "sample_rate": 16000, "channels": 1, "language": "en"}`
  2. Server replies with `{"type": "ready", ...}`.
  3. Send binary frames containing little-endian int16 PCM samples at the declared sample rate.
  4. Server emits `{"type": "partial", "text": ...}` messages every ~chunk_seconds.
  5. Send `{"type": "stop"}` (or close) to finalize. Server returns `{"type": "final", "text": ..., "segments": [...]}`.

Postman cannot record microphone audio, so use `tests/test_live_mic.py` (Python) provided with this service to exercise this endpoint.

item.name: SmartDischargePlannerService
item.description:
Postman collection for Smart Discharge Planner Service REST API.

This service accepts clinical and operational patient data and returns an AI-generated, structured discharge readiness assessment (readiness status, blockers, medication reconciliation concerns, follow-up considerations, and a draft discharge summary).

The collection includes:
- Health Check
- Plan Discharge (Minimal) — smallest valid payload
- Plan Discharge (Full Example) — every optional field populated with a single representative entry per list
- Plan Discharge (Comprehensive Example) — a realistic, fully-populated multi-condition patient encounter with multiple entries across every list field, plus a saved example response showing the full shape of a real AI-generated discharge plan
- Plan Discharge (Invalid Payload) — demonstrates 422 validation error shape

Each request includes a saved example response under its "Examples" tab in Postman so you can see expected output without needing a live OpenAI-backed server running.

request.description:
A realistic, fully-populated multi-condition patient encounter exercising every field in the request schema with multiple entries per list (7 vitals, 4 pending tests, 3 active problems, 5 current and 6 discharge medications, 4 clinical notes of different types, 4 follow-up appointments across specialties, 5 patient education topics, and 4 equipment needs).

Patient profile: pneumonia with diabetes, hypertension, COPD, and CKD stage 3 comorbidities, improving but with several unresolved discharge blockers (pending cultures, unconfirmed home oxygen, unscheduled specialist follow-up). This is the best example to use for understanding the full range of realistic input the service can accept and reason over.
